_comment: Written by the trading runs. impliedMove is a decimal or null. null means the straddle was not pulled - an open checklist item, not a placeholder to guess at. This file is a list of what is AHEAD: the pre-close run prunes catalysts once their date has passed and re-reads spot from a live quote, because a reference price carried from the day it was written makes every implied range wrong.
prunedNote: PRUNED AGAINST A LIVE CALENDAR AND, FOR THE FIRST TIME IN SIX SESSIONS, THE ANSWER IS NOT AN EMPTY FILE. The earnings calendar was re-pulled live across 2026-08-18 to 2026-08-26. NOTHING WAS REMOVED because the file carried no rows, and NO CARRIED SPOT NEEDED REFRESHING for the same reason - both duties are recorded as performed rather than skipped, which is the distinction this note exists to preserve. WHAT THE PULL FOUND. First, that three names this board watches printed THIS MORNING - AS, KLAR and BIDU - and are therefore behind it rather than ahead of it; a report that has already happened is not an anticipated move and none of the three is entered here. Second, that of the twelve watched names NOT ONE has a dated event of its own anywhere in the window: not SMCI, UPST, AMD, IONQ, RGTI, SOUN, OKLO, SMR or JOBY. That is the sixth consecutive session in which a live pull has floored the entire watch list on the catalyst question rather than ranking it. Third, and the reason this file is no longer blank: NVDA reports 2026-08-26 after the close, verified on the live calendar, six sessions out. No watched name owns that event and this board would not be trading NVDA - one share is 21.7% of the account and the option chain is far outside reach - but the 2026-08-10 rule change was written specifically about a correlated AI complex that leads together and unwinds together, and AMD sits on the candidate list. A file whose whole purpose is to say what is ahead cannot be empty when the largest dated event in that complex is six sessions away. So it is entered as a REGIME row rather than a trade row, with its branches decided now. SPOT IS LIVE, NOT CARRIED: 219.22 bid at 19:37:21.420Z, pulled in the same call as every other quote this run took, which is the failure mode this file exists to prevent - AMD sat on this board at 522.95 the morning it traded at 486. IMPLIED MOVE IS NULL AND THAT IS AN OPEN CHECKLIST ITEM RATHER THAN A PLACEHOLDER: no straddle was pulled, this board holds nothing into the print, and a straddle quoted six sessions early is not the number that will govern on 8/25 - the pre-close of 8/25 owns pulling it, and the 8/27 open owns pruning this row.

moves.source: Spot pulled live at 19:37:21.420Z on 8/18 in the same single call as this run's AS, SMCI, KLAR and AMD quotes, so it shares one timestamp with the rest of the board's reads: 219.22 bid / 219.24 ask on a 0.009% spread, last trade 219.21, against a 225.01 close on 8/17 - down 2.57% on the day. The event was verified on a live earnings-calendar pull covering 2026-08-18 to 2026-08-26: NVDA, 2026-08-26, timing pm, verified true, no actual yet, estimate 2.07 for fiscal Q2 2027. impliedMove is null because NO STRADDLE WAS PULLED - this board holds nothing into the print, item 3 is owed only before an earnings hold, and a straddle quoted six sessions early measures a different event than the one that will be priced on 8/25. The 8/25 pre-close owns pulling it if anything is open or contemplated by then. AMD is recorded here as the transmission mechanism rather than as a second row: 482.38 bid at 19:37:20.737Z, -4.67% on the day, and one share is 47.8% of a 1009.16 account against the 40% single-name ceiling, so AMD is refused by an explicit mechanical limit before any view about NVDA reaches it.

branches.cond: An entry considered in the AI or semiconductor complex - AMD, SMCI, or any sympathy name - on 8/25 or 8/26, into the print
branches.act: Refused, decided now rather than on the day
branches.why: The rulebook forbids holding an option through a print outright, and for equity the -8% stop has to survive the event or it is not a stop. This board has already refused SMCI once on exactly that arithmetic - a 14.4% implied move swallows an 8% stop, so the realistic bad case gaps through the exit rather than filling at it. NVDA's own move is not the exposure here; the exposure is that a sympathy name carries the index's gap without carrying its liquidity, which is the 2026-08-10 finding about four names off one list being one position at four times the size. Writing the refusal down six sessions early is the point: on 8/26 it would be a view about the report, and today it is a mechanical consequence of a stop that cannot hold.

branches.cond: A position from an unrelated setup is open and running into 8/26
branches.act: The 8/26 pre-close decides it explicitly against this row, and a hold through the print requires the straddle pulled first
branches.why: A name outside the complex is not automatically exposed, and this row must not become a reason to close good positions early on a date that has nothing to do with them. But an NVDA print is the one evening a session where correlation appears in names that showed none for a month, so the hold cannot be passive. Item 3 binds: no straddle pulled means no earnings hold, and that applies to a position held THROUGH the event even when the event belongs to another ticker whose gap it will wear.

branches.cond: The complex sells off into 8/26 and a name on this board looks cheap for it
branches.act: Not bought on that basis, and re-approached only from 8/27 on the reaction bar
branches.why: Cheapness ahead of a dated binary is not a setup - it is the binary being priced, and buying it is taking the event risk the branch above just refused. This is the same reasoning that has kept KLAR unbought through a 22% gap all day: the first print of a fall is not a support level. The post-print session is the first point the rulebook can engage at all, and item 2 then governs - the reaction day is not the entry, the day-2 or day-3 pullback that holds is.
